summary: alipclutch-baileys ships char-code-obfuscated exfiltration endpoint in messaging send path
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. In lib/Socket/messages-send.js line 425 (and again at line 436) the code reconstructs a hardcoded destination host from a String.fromCharCode(...) decimal array; the decoded value is the URL https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The destination is hidden via char-code decoding rather than appearing as a plain string in source, is not a WhatsApp/Baileys endpoint, and is not caller-configurable. Wiring an obfuscated third-party host into the messaging send path of a WhatsApp client library exfiltrates or mirrors caller message data / session material to an attacker-controlled destination whenever the consumer's session sends messages.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
